A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIRD framework and research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, human evaluations of probabilities and follow-up questions, supervision-transfer results, ablations, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and adds a loss-component ablation in Appendix A.9, Table 8.

M1.justification: The Bayesian model, objectives, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, but the supplied inference prompts change operationally. Figure 8 replaces single-statement entailment with factor-value selection, an explicit None option, and tie-breaking; Figure 9 replaces strict removal of unsupported values with a more lenient deletion rule.

E1.justification: Both versions use COMMON2SENSE, TODAY, and PLASMA, with MATRES and TRACIE retained for supervision-transfer evaluation. The new loss ablation uses existing tasks; the revised scenario count does not establish new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The established Vanilla, Logit, CoT, EC, and existing ablation comparators are retained. New Table 8 adds two evaluated comparison variants, BIRD without MR loss and BIRD without MSE loss.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.4 change the reported COMMON2SENSE scenario count from 213 to 216, retaining 3,822 instances. Sections 4.2 and A.5 remove the stated filter requiring every method to make correct binary decisions, retaining 350 evaluation examples. This revises the reported selection protocol without establishing a rerun. Table 8 also introduces loss-removal controls.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.9 tests whether each component of the existing two-loss objective contributes to decision accuracy. Table 8 reports separate MR-loss and MSE-loss removals across three datasets using Llama-3.1-70b. Earlier factor-generation ablations, probability-assignment ablations, and error analyses remain.

E5.justification: The versions retain point-estimate reporting and the human-annotation replication procedures. The added ablation introduces no experimental seed reporting, run-to-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Llama-3.1 CoT average F1 from 0.346 to 0.309, with all three class scores also revised, and changes fixed-initial-probability Different1 F1 from 0.616 to 0.614. New Table 8 adds six loss-ablation scores. Other benchmark and follow-up results are retained. The revised selection description prevents assuming strict same-setting comparability for Table 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations (1)-(13), Appendix A.1 derivation, and A.2 assumptions are substantively unchanged. The parameter-count expression added in A.3 makes the existing parameterization explicit rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about reliable probability estimation, interpretable and controllable Bayesian inference, decision making, soft supervision, and follow-up questions. The additional ablation supports the existing framework without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly characterizes 128 samples as a training minimum, suggests more samples improve alignment, and provides an expert-informed Likert-scale rationale for probability mappings, including claimed insensitivity to small adjustments. A.9 adds the interpretation that both losses are crucial. Existing failure analyses remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability link, discloses grid-search tuning using a PLASMA validation set, clarifies scenario-specific parameters and training samples, and explains the temporal training underlying Table 3 in new A.10. Prompt templates are revised. Conversely, Section 4.1 removes the general temperature-0.7 statement.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain unchanged. DeLLMa's reference changes from its 2024 preprint to its 2025 ICLR publication, which is a bibliographic update to the same work.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted language and terminology corrections, rewrites several prompt examples, adds acknowledgements and two appendix subsections, and updates the publication header. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the loss-ablation Table 8, relocates Figure 2 before Related Work, and revises its caption and several prompt boxes. The existing follow-up-question table becomes Table 9, with unchanged results. These are localized display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies separate loss-component evidence absent from v2 and adds useful code-access, tuning, and training explanations. These provide limited gains in evidential support and reproducibility while the central results and theory remain stable. The unexplained evaluation-selection revision and removed general temperature statement temper the improvement.
